chapter: Musicians he knew and played with
title: Piano players in the Miramac band
summary: Punch struggles to name the band's several pianists and recalls James Hemingway as a good one.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who was the piano player with you?

Well, we had two, three, had a girl. That girl I told him about went nuts, Laura. Laura. Made her a long time. Then we had a fellow named Brownie, Clowns Brownie. Oh, two, three piano players. They didn't keep no good piano. Oh yeah, the boy died. James, James from Atlanta, Georgia. Johnson, James P. No, James, put James down, I'll call his name. He was a dope thing, he died. Not James, James, James from Atlanta, Georgia. Johnson, James P. No, James, put James down, I'll call his name. He was a dope thing till he died. Not James, I think that James Cadbury. Not James, see, James something.
Did Morris Rouse ever work with him? Who? Morris Rouse, Rouse, what can I pronounce it, Rouse or Rouse? Never knew him, huh?
Hemingway, James Hemingway. Hemingway. Yeah, James Hemingway. Now he was a good piano player.
